newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-JOCKEYS CLEARED OVER FAILURE TO RACE.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-JOCKEYS CLEARED OVER FAILURE TO RACE.

text.p: Twenty jockeys who failed to continue racing in October last year on what they considered was dangerous ground at Britain's Haydock Park were exonerated by the country's racing authorities on Thursday.
But Frankie Dettori, the man who rode seven winners from seven rides at Ascot last season, was found in breach of the rules.
However, officials from the Jockey Club, the sport's ruling disciplinary body, decided to take no action against him.
Racing was abandoned at Haydock on October 16 after just one race after a group of senior jockeys and racing officials inspected the course.
Many of the jockeys, including Dettori, who flew in from Dubai, gave evidence at the two-day hearing.
Some riders said the race cancellation had not been a boycott but resulted from a communication breakdown between jockeys and racing officials.
A statement issued by Jockey Club on Thursday said the committee had found that all the jockeys had been prepared to ride, with the exception of Dettori.
It said: "The jockeys were adamant that there had not been a 'strike' as had been reported, and the committee was satisfied there was not a collective decision to refuse to ride."
Champion jockey Pat Eddery said afterwards: "I am delighted. It was a very good decision. It was just an unfortunate misunderstanding."
